recommended_title: How Far Can Five Cheap Graph Statistics Go? Log-Linear Cover-Time Prediction on Small Connected Graphs
central_question: For connected graphs with 6<=n<=30, does a ridge model on a handful of cheap graph statistics (n, m, mean degree, max degree, diameter) predict Monte Carlo start-averaged random-walk cover time with lower family-macro log error than the generic 2m(n-1) bound?
central_thesis: On the sealed held-out graphs, a five-statistic log-linear ridge predictor (family-macro log MAE 0.181) is far closer to Monte Carlo cover times than the 2m(n-1) bound (1.754) and than constant and label-shuffled controls (0.870, 1.423), with median Monte Carlo relative SE about 0.029; this is measured only on 12 synthetic families, 24 test graphs, and the question of which families it fails on is not answered by the retained evidence.
narrative_rationale: The only grounded, completed evidence is the sealed final evaluation (outcome qualified, status completed) of the frozen selection, which is the seed baseline ridge predictor (study.selection_kind=baseline; investigation completed_no_winner; 1 attempt, 0 scored, 1 unscored; search score delta 0.0). The strongest honest story is therefore a calibrated, narrow empirical-measurement paper: a cheap-statistic log-linear predictor versus the worst-case bound and sanity controls, with explicit scope limits. No improvement over a baseline is claimed because the studied method IS the baseline; the unscored resistance/Matthews variant has no performance evidence and is not a result. The second half of the research question (error vs graph type) cannot be answered quantitatively because per-family metrics are absent from paper_data; the paper must say so (unknown, not a failure) and use the family design only as a description of the test distribution and as a stated limitation/future-work item.
edit_framing_decision: Not edit mode: no previous_paper or staged inputs exist (edit-context placeholders are unfilled), so there is no prior story to preserve or replace; field value is nominal. Fresh thesis-first framing chosen over a Matthews/resistance-predictor story, which lacks any scored evidence.
staged_input_impact: No staged paper, program, or result inputs were provided; framing is based solely on paper_data.json final_evaluation and downstream_study.

method_groups.name: Five-statistic log-linear ridge predictor (frozen selection)
method_groups.include_reason: This is the studied method (frozen selection = seed baseline program): standardized log n, log m, log mean degree, log max degree, log diameter; ridge (lambda=1, unpenalised intercept) on log cover time, fit in-episode on labelled training graphs; exact method visible in source_evidence/downstream/program/src/program.py.

method_groups.name: Generic 2m(n-1) worst-case bound
method_groups.include_reason: The comparator named in the research question (Aleliunas et al.); final bound macro log MAE 1.754. Also the fallback when no training data is supplied.

method_groups.name: Constant predictor control
method_groups.include_reason: Family-agnostic sanity control (0.870); shows the gain is not just calibrating the overall scale.

method_groups.name: Label-shuffled control
method_groups.include_reason: Negative control (1.423) showing the ridge fit uses the statistic-to-target relation rather than fitting artefacts. Describe only as the evaluator's shuffled-label control; do not invent finer feature ablations.

method_groups.name: Relabeling-invariance check
method_groups.include_reason: perm_max_rel_dev=0.0 documents that predictions depend only on relabeling-invariant statistics (validity check, not a performance claim).

results_focus: Single direct comparison of family-macro log MAE (sealed final): ridge 0.181 vs constant 0.870, shuffled 1.423, 2m(n-1) bound 1.754; improvement_vs_bound 1.572 (consistent with 1.754-0.181).

Monte Carlo uncertainty: median relative SE of labels ~0.029 (log-scale ~0.03 order), much smaller than the 0.181 model error, so label noise is a minor part of the measured error; present as a noise-floor context, not as a confidence interval on the model score.

Episode variability: 3 seeded episodes (201-203) all gave identical score -0.18137 (deterministic candidate, fixed test graphs/labels) so episode-to-episode spread is zero and must NOT be presented as sampling uncertainty over graphs; state that uncertainty over graph draws was not measured.

Qualification: outcome qualified, status completed, correct=true (final.qualification.*); candidate_diagnostics_trust is 'unverified' - disclose. No failed gates to discuss; do not claim validity beyond the reported qualification.

Scope and unknowns: per-family errors, per-size errors, and which families the predictor fails on are NOT available; write as an explicit open item. Describe the test set composition (12 families, 2 test graphs each, 24 total; 36 final train graphs, 3 per family) only if drawn from the task evaluator/resources and phrase as design description.

Search vs final separation: search baseline score -0.1913 (delta 0.0, 0 of 1 attempts scored) is a different evaluation scope from final -0.1814; do not compare them as an improvement. Unscored attempt = missing evidence.

forbidden_phrases: our proposed method outperforms the baseline
notes_for_writer: The studied method is the frozen selection = the seed baseline; never call it a novel winner or an improvement over a baseline. The comparison is against the 2m(n-1) bound and controls, all evaluated in the same sealed final run.

Do not state which graph families are reliable or failing: no per-family metric is grounded. Say the family-dependence question is unresolved by retained evidence and frame it as the key limitation/future work. You may describe the 12-family design as scope.

Do not claim generality beyond n in [6,30], start-averaged cover time, 12 synthetic families, 24 final test graphs (2 per family) - a connectivity smoke-test scale. Derived ratios (e.g., ridge error is about one fifth of the constant control's and about a tenth of the bound's) are allowed if labeled as arithmetic on the reported metrics.

Do not present the zero spread over episodes 201-203 as confidence; explain it arises from a deterministic predictor on fixed graphs/labels. Report MC uncertainty only via mc_rel_se_median (median relative SE 0.0287).
Mention the Matthews/effective-resistance predictor only, at most, as an untested future direction (1 attempt, unscored); do not report numbers for it.
Report that the final candidate-diagnostics trust is 'unverified' and that qualification (qualified/completed) is an evaluator outcome, not a proof of validity beyond it.

Body budget 8-9 ICLR pages with thin evidence: spend space on (a) precise problem framing and why 2m(n-1)=sum-over-edges bound is loose on small graphs, (b) full method specification enabling reimplementation, (c) metric/aggregation design and why clipped log error is used, (d) a careful threats-to-validity and limitations section (small test set, family confound, deterministic episodes, distribution shift of sizes, labels are MC estimates), (e) related work on Aleliunas et al., Feige, Lovasz. No padding; if the evidence cannot honestly fill 8 pages, prefer substantive discussion over invented experiments.

Cite only entries in references.bib (Feige upper/lower bound entries present; verify others before citing). Starter literature (Aleliunas et al., Lovasz survey) must be cited only if present in references.bib.
Figure export: PDF and 300 DPI PNG from source; reference the PDF in LaTeX; if raster-only, >=2400 px for full width; never upscale. Only one figure uses generate-concept-figure (overview).
